Hi Sergio, it is Marina. A quick note before Thursday. I read Nordbank's reply twice. Three asks went out and two of them came back in a shape we can live with, so let us be very clear about which one still matters. The ceiling is the one you cannot drop. The grace period is already granted and the fee is small, so do not spend the call on either of them. On the fee, my view is simple. Give it to them. Say we accept the one percent, and in return ask them to take the ceiling to our benchmark and to put the grace period in writing the day we sign. That is a clean trade and he can sell it to his committee. Where you hold firm is the ceiling, and only the ceiling. One more thing. Please do not use the words walk away on this call. Keep that card in your pocket. We play it only if the number is still there on Friday, and even then I want to hear it from you first. Good luck.

Sergio, it is Paulo from the credit desk. One thought about Thursday, and it is not about the numbers. The way you phrase the ask decides how much room the other side has to say yes. If you say we need the ceiling at two hundred, that is an order, and the poor man on the other end has to defend a position instead of solving a problem. If you say would you be able to take the ceiling to two hundred, he can walk into his committee and argue for you. Same number, completely different conversation. Second thing, the package. Never ask for three things one at a time, because they say no three times and then there is nothing left to trade. Put them on the table together and say which one matters most. And the last thing, about goodwill. Thank him for the grace period before you push on the ceiling. It costs you nothing and it buys you the tone for the rest of the call. Talk on Friday.

First, thank the other side for what they have already granted. Then put all your asks on the table together, not one at a time. Next, say which one matters most and why. After that, offer something in return, so they can sell the answer internally. Finally, ask for a clear next step and a date.
